"Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table."
Labelled design judgement; the lesson states it with conditions ("roughly", "only pays off if ..."). No version-dependent fact inside.

Judgement, but its factual base checks out: multi-shop-data-rollout.md l.58-61 puts per-service PostgreSQL roles and per-service RabbitMQ users in the same step 3 of release 3; splitting broker users involves no RLS step. threat-model.md l.80-81 gives the grouping reason.

Ledger calls it opinion, but it is PostgreSQL behaviour. Docs: "No privileges are granted to PUBLIC by default on tables..."; databases get CONNECT for PUBLIC, so a non-superuser role with no grants connects and its SELECT fails with a permission error, as the lesson says.
